author: WP12
summary: Updated for the Bible's pin: the resolution ladder, root and containment rules, cache identity, ownership, failure and concurrency boundaries, service provider, ResourceContentManager, TitleContainer, the manifest and the media readers. Stale at TARGET in its caching table (no weak Texture2D cache, TextureCube cached), in claiming the service provider is never consulted, in the Video platform exclusions and in the SoundEffect decode route. The site's guide, runtime internals and handbook already held the ladder and error mapping; the exact spelling consequences, containment bases, reentrancy hazards, Game assignment semantics, manifest caveats and media-reader probing now live on a new deep dive.

concepts.text: ContentManager maps a logical name plus the requested C++ type to an XNB object, a compiled CNB object, a CNJ object or a native loose asset; its defining rule is selection, not decoding.
The runtime ContentManager and the build-time Content Pipeline are separate modules: the manager only consumes what cna-content writes and never runs an importer.
tokens: The runtime ContentManager on this page is the consumer of that output

concepts.text: On a cache miss the manager builds base = BuildAssetPath(name) and tries base.xnb, then base.cnb, then a name that itself ends in .cnb, then asks the loose reader for T to take the literal path, base.cnj, and its declared extensions in order, falling back to the bare path so the reader reports what is missing.

Existence selects the candidate and decoding never retries: a malformed XNB, invalid CNB or CNJ, corrupt literal file, a directory carrying the asset's name, or a corrupt first native extension stops the load without trying a lower-priority sibling.
tokens: a directory that happens to carry the asset's name

concepts.text: XNB has first priority so that externally produced XNA assets are never shadowed by CNA conveniences; CNB follows because it is CNA's own compiled output and must outrank every source the pipeline compiles from.
tokens: CNB ranks below XNB and above everything CNA can compile from

concepts.text: Only a caller-spelled .cnb suffix gets a literal compiled tier; a spelled .xnb suffix does not.
tokens: The one suffix the manager recognises

concepts.text: The XNB tier reads through TryReadAssetBytes, which also consults the platform's case-insensitive file loader (packaged Android assets), while the CNB and loose tiers use std::filesystem::exists and plain streams; .cnb loading from an Android package is unverified.
tokens: whether a .cnb inside an Android package loads has not been established

concepts.text: Because the XNB probe appends .xnb to the complete name, Load<Texture2D>("art/logo.png") first tests art/logo.png.xnb and art/logo.png.cnb, then the literal PNG; spelling art/logo.xnb hands the XNB bytes to the image decoder, which fails.
tokens: The XNB bytes are handed to the image decoder

concepts.text: Dots in logical names have no special meaning: existence rather than has_extension() is tested so a localized name such as Flag.en-US still gets reader extensions appended.

With hero.png and hero.cnj side by side, Load("sprites/hero.png") reads the literal PNG while Load("sprites/hero") selects hero.cnj before the native extensions (unless hero.xnb or hero.cnb exist); the two results are separate cache entries.

A CNJ sourceFile starts a checked nested Load<T> of the resolved logical name, which walks the full ladder again (a hero.png.xnb would win) and is cached under its own key; it is not a direct decoder bypass.
tokens: That nested call is a full, checked load

concepts.text: An empty asset name is not rejected by Load<T>: BuildAssetPath returns the root, so the root directory itself becomes the literal candidate and the loose reader fails on it; only the protected ReadAsset<T> refuses an empty name with ArgumentNullException.
tokens: An empty name is not rejected up front

concepts.text: Native extensions tried after the literal and CNJ candidates: Texture2D .png .jpg .jpeg .bmp .gif .tga .tif .tiff .qoi; TextureCube .dds; SoundEffect .wav; Song .mp3 .ogg .wav .flac .opus .aac .wma; Video .mp4 .ogv .webm .mkv .avi .mov; Model .cnj .gltf .glb; SpriteFont, Effect, AnimationClipEXT, Curve and Texture3D .cnj only.
The Model reader lists .cnj first in its own GetExtensions(), which is redundant with the manager-level CNJ probe and harmless.

Claim that the loose Video reader is excluded on Emscripten, Android and MinGW: at the snapshot VideoTypeReader is registered in every build; without the FFmpeg backend its raw-file constructor throws NotSupportedException, which the loose tier wraps, while XNB/CNB videos load metadata and fail only at Play.
tokens: the loose Video reader is registered in every build
concepts.note: Bible listed platform exclusions; TARGET registers the reader unconditionally and fails at construction without a backend.

concepts.text: The global .cnj probe runs even for readers that do not understand CNJ: loose Song and Video treat the selected path as media, so an extensionless name with a same-named .cnj yields a Song or Video pointing at the JSON file; pass the explicit media file name.
tokens: returns a Song whose file is the JSON document
Pass the explicit media file name

concepts.text: RootDirectory is a base path, not a sandbox: BuildAssetPath joins root and name after turning backslashes into slashes, without rejecting absolute names, collapsing dot segments or checking symlinks; an absolute name replaces the root.
tokens: RootDirectory is a base path, not a sandbox
an absolute name replaces the root

concepts.text: The accepted absolute outside-root name is a stated contract: the helper that maps resolved sidecar paths back to logical names documents that Load accepts an explicit absolute outside-root asset.
tokens: by established contract, an explicit absolute outside-root asset

concepts.text: Top-level names therefore must be trusted or validated by the application; only references written inside content are contained.
tokens: joins the root and the caller's name without a containment check

concepts.text: CNJ sourceFile rejects empty and absolute values, targets outside the root after weakly_canonical component-wise comparison (symlink escapes), another .cnj, and a target whose sibling .cnj exists (implicit cycles).
ContentReader::ReadExternalReference rejects absolute, drive-qualified and UNC spellings and lexically normalised results above the root, while allowing sibling ../ references.

XNB Song and Video readers contain their companion media within the root, checking the stored spelling and again the extension-probed file; for an explicitly loaded outside-root XNB the XNB's own folder becomes the authorized bundle root.
tokens: The chosen file is contained a second time

concepts.text: Paths inside documents use three different bases: sourceFile relative to the .cnj's folder, most CNJ sidecar fields relative to the content root, and .skinnedmodel.json fields relative to the manifest's folder.
tokens: Three different bases for paths inside documents

concepts.text: The containment checks compare canonicalised paths before the later open; they are not an open-by-handle policy, so the time-of-check to time-of-use window remains.
NormalizeKey converts backslashes to slashes and lowercases every byte with std::tolower; it does not include the root, resolve dot segments or canonicalise a file.
Consequences of textual keys: Sprites\Logo and sprites/logo share an entry; textures/../logo and logo occupy two entries; case-distinct files on a case-sensitive filesystem collapse to one key.
tokens: two files that differ only in case

concepts.text: Changing RootDirectory does not invalidate an already cached logical name; call Unload before reusing names under a new root.
tokens: does not invalidate the cached entry

concepts.text: A direct Texture2D constructor with a concrete path and device (Texture2D("assets/logo.png", getGraphicsDeviceProperty())) remains available for small programs; it decodes one file with no ladder, cache or containment.
tokens: with no ladder, cache or containment

concepts.text: A Game exposes its configured manager through getContentProperty(); a game sets the root with setRootDirectoryProperty and loads by value with Load<T>.
RegisterTypeReader<T> installs one loose reader per C++ type on one manager; RegisterCnjLoader<T> installs named CNJ factories for a type without a reader; register before loading begins.
Successful generic loads enter one strong cache keyed by requested type and normalised name, written only after the reader returns, so a failed top-level load leaves no entry and can be retried.
tokens: the cache is written only after a reader returns

concepts.text: Claim that Texture2D keeps a weak renderer cache and that TextureCube is uncached: at the snapshot there is no weak texture cache; Texture2D and TextureCube (copyable, shared renderer) are cached like other types, and only SoundEffect is uncached.
tokens: There is no separate weak texture cache at this snapshot
which is copyable, is cached like any other type
concepts.note: Bible table described Texture2D/TextureCube specialisations removed before TARGET (weak cache removed by commit 975156d14).

concepts.text: Repeated loads return copies of the cached value; for GPU-backed XNA value types and shared_ptr assets the cache and every caller share the underlying object, so caller-held values outlive eviction.
tokens: the cache and every caller share one underlying object

concepts.text: SoundEffect is move-only with a per-owner dispose cascade, so its explicit specialisation decodes an independently owned value on every call and caches nothing.
Unload clears only the generic cache: it disposes nothing, does not revoke held copies, and leaves readers, CNJ loaders, root, device, provider and manifest untouched.
tokens: leaves the loose readers, the CNJ loader table

concepts.text: Dispose routes to Dispose(true), which unloads once and marks the manager; later Load<T> throws std::runtime_error, ReadAsset<T> throws ObjectDisposedException, and a second Dispose does nothing.
The C++ destructor is defaulted and does not call Dispose; a derived manager overriding Dispose(bool) must add using ContentManager::Dispose because the declaration hides the public overload.
Nested reader activity is not transactional: dependencies loaded by a reader enter the cache immediately and remain if the outer reader fails afterwards.
tokens: Nested loads are neither transactional nor cycle-checked

concepts.text: No provisional key or cycle detector exists, so by reading a self-referencing chain (for example an EffectMaterial XNB whose effect reference names its own asset) re-enters Load until stack exhaustion; only CNJ sourceFile refuses cycles.
tokens: Nothing marks a name as in progress

concepts.text: Game::setContentProperty performs a memberwise copy assignment into the game's own manager (cache, readers, CNJ loaders, manifest, disposed flag, root, raw provider and device pointers) instead of replacing an object reference as FNA does.
tokens: copy-assigns into the game's own member

concepts.text: Assigning a standalone manager that never received setGraphicsDevice replaces the game's device pointer with null; to change only the root, configure the existing manager in place (Unload, then setRootDirectoryProperty).
tokens: replaces the game's device pointer with null

concepts.text: ContentLoadException covers validated content errors (malformed XNB/CNB/CNJ, missing reader, bad indices, unsupported reader versions) but is not a universal wrapper; the XNB tier leaves EndOfStreamException, bad_any_cast and object-construction exceptions unwrapped.
The loose tier wraps any std::exception from a reader in ContentLoadException with an inner cause and passes ContentLoadException through; the SoundEffect specialisation's loose tier does not wrap.
tokens: The SoundEffect specialization's loose tier does not wrap

concepts.text: Wrong T for a .cnb is a ContentLoadException naming both types, but it is raised after the loader has already built the object, because the check is an any_cast of the produced value.
tokens: raised after the loader has already built the object

concepts.text: A failing Song companion in an XNB surfaces as System::IO::FileNotFoundException, and device or profile refusals during XNB object creation (Texture3D on Reach, an inexpressible vertex declaration) surface as NotSupportedException, both unwrapped.
Callers that must survive bad content catch ContentLoadException for validated errors and std::exception for the unwrapped tiers (example with LevelData).
The manager's maps, manifest vector, strings, pointers and disposed flag are unsynchronised; concurrent load, unload, registration, root or manifest operations are data races.
Single-thread reentrancy hazards exist: self-loading cycles have no sentinel and a reader that replaces its own registration during Read destroys the object that is executing.
Rule: register readers and configure first, serialise manager mutation through one owner, and hand completed assets to workers.
tokens: from one owner, and hand finished assets to workers

concepts.text: Claim that the IServiceProvider constructors keep a raw pointer that the manager never consults: at the snapshot getGraphicsDeviceInternal falls back to GetService(IGraphicsDeviceService) when no device pointer was set, then throws ContentLoadException.
concepts.note: Bible said GetService is never called; TARGET calls it as the fallback.

concepts.text: A GPU-backed standalone manager needs an explicit device (setGraphicsDevice) and, outside a Game, a call to RegisterAllBuiltInXnbReaders; Game performs both for its own manager and both pointers stay borrowed.

None of the three constructors rejects a null service provider, unlike XNA's which throw ArgumentNullException; ContentManager(IServiceProvider*) leaves the root empty while ContentManager() and the Game's manager use "Content".
tokens: none of the three constructors rejects a null provider

concepts.text: The protected OpenStream and ReadAsset<T> seams exist; the base OpenStream reads <root>/<name>.xnb through TryReadAssetBytes, but Load<T> never calls OpenStream, so only ReadAsset<T> honours an override.
tokens: OpenStream is not on the Load<T> path

concepts.text: ResourceContentManager's two-argument constructor requires a ResourceManager (ArgumentNullException otherwise); its OpenStream looks up the named binary resource with distinct ContentLoadException paths for no resource family, not found, not binary and too large.
tokens: not found, not binary and too large

concepts.text: Focused tests cover the seam: ContentRuntimeContractTests (ReadAsset through an overridden OpenStream, cache untouched, disposables handed to the recorder) and ResourceContentManagerTests.

TitleContainer::OpenStream is an independent direct-file helper that ContentManager never calls; it normalises backslashes, resolves relative names against TitleLocation and returns a read stream, with an Android platform-loader fallback copied into a MemoryStream.
tokens: ContentManager does not open assets through TitleContainer

concepts.text: TitleContainer resolution is lexical rather than contained: rooted names are used as given and relative names are joined to TitleLocation with lexically_normal, so .. segments, absolute paths and symlinks can leave the title folder; it suits application-controlled paths only.
tokens: it is meant for application-controlled paths

concepts.text: The CNAEXT TitleLocation path setter is mutable, process-global and unsynchronised.
tokens: Its cached static state is not synchronized

concepts.text: GetContentManifest lazily scans the root and returns a reference to manager-owned rows; RefreshContentManifest rebuilds them; GetXnbReaderUsageSummary aggregates reader names with a registered flag.
The manifest is diagnostic only: Load never consults it, presence proves no validity, compressed or malformed XNBs show empty reader lists, and .cnb is listed as a native extension.
tokens: the manifest does not model the CNB tier

concepts.text: Manifest row and summary order is unstable (unordered_map iteration), a missing root yields an empty snapshot with no scan status, a refresh invalidates held references and iterators, and Unload, disposal and root changes do not refresh it.
tokens: A refresh invalidates references and iterators

concepts.text: Loose Song and Video readers simply wrap the selected media path (Video also needs the manager's device), while the XNB readers decode the XNA body and resolve an external companion.

The XNB SoundEffectReader takes PCM16 directly; PCM8, IEEE float, IMA-ADPCM and MS-ADPCM are handled and XMA2 is refused; MS-ADPCM without a coefficient table receives the standard one and a block-derived samples-per-block value.
tokens: XMA2 and unknown tags are refused
concepts.note: Bible routed PCM8/float/ADPCM through SDL's decoder; TARGET keeps PCM8 native and decodes the rest with CNA's own DecodeWavToPcm16.

concepts.text: An XNB Song body holds a reference string and a duration in milliseconds; the reader contains the reference, strips the final four characters when long enough and probes the stem, .ogg, .oga and .qoa, restoring the stored spelling when none exists.
tokens: falling back to the stored spelling

concepts.text: The probe preserves the desktop convention of shipping an .ogg beside an XNA .wma placeholder; it is not general extension parsing.
tokens: it is not general extension parsing

concepts.text: Song construction checks that the chosen file exists, so a well-formed XNB without its companion fails during Load<Song> with FileNotFoundException; decoding is deferred to playback.
The retained MonoGame Song fixture (one_two_three.xnb with its .ogg) establishes XNB dispatch, sibling lookup, duration and the .ogg route, not playback or the other probes.
A pipeline-produced Song writes its duration as an Int32Reader object (two-entry table) while CNA's older fixtures wrote a bare Int32; the reader distinguishes them by table size.
tokens: the reader tells them apart by the table size

concepts.text: An XNB Video body contains reference, duration, width, height, frame rate and soundtrack type; the reader contains the reference, probes stem, .ogv and .ogg, and stores the metadata without opening or validating the media.

VideoPlayer::Play performs the decoder open: without a video backend it throws NotSupportedException, an unopenable file leaves the player stopped without the FNA-style exception, and a size or frame-rate mismatch beyond 1 fps throws InvalidOperationException.
The strongest Video test uses a test-built XNB and CNA's FFmpeg fixture; no externally produced Video XNB is retained.
tokens: no externally produced Video XNB is committed

concepts.text: Porting rules: use extensionless names when compiled or sidecar precedence is wanted and literal names when the native file must win (always for Song and Video); treat RootDirectory and TitleContainer as trusted-path conveniences; register readers and attach a device first; serialise manager mutation; Unload before changing the cache namespace.

Existing XNA/FNA compiled assets load only for reader families present at the snapshot; compiled Effect bytecode is a separate, renderer-qualified contract, with CNB, CNJ or native conversion as the route where a reader or renderer route is missing.
tokens: compiled Effect bytecode additionally needs a renderer build that reports

concepts.text: Summary: ContentManager is a deterministic existence-priority resolver with type-specific caching; XNB, literal, CNJ and native candidates are not fallbacks after decode failure, which explains explicit filename choice, cache-hidden root changes, sidecars shadowing native media and a manifest that inventories without certifying.

issues.text: Load<Song>/Load<Video> with an extensionless name select a same-named .cnj and build a media object pointing at the JSON file.
ContentManager::Unload() disposes nothing; held assets stay valid through shared ownership, unlike XNA's disposing Unload.
ResourceContentManager::OpenStream is implemented; Load<T> still never routes through OpenStream, so the override is reached only by ReadAsset<T>.
No in-progress marker in Load<T>: a self-referencing XNB chain (EffectMaterial effect reference, untyped external references) recurses until stack exhaustion.
A loose reader that re-registers its own T during Read destroys the executing reader object (Load<T> holds a reference into typeReaders_).
Game::setContentProperty copy-assigns a manager, which can overwrite the game's device pointer with null when the source manager has no device.
Windows video include guard in ContentManager.cpp mismatching the CMake exclusion: at TARGET the file has no video guard and the Video types link in every build.
SongTypeReader advertises .opus/.aac/.wma; whether the selected audio backend can decode them was not established for this package.
Loading .cnb from an Android packaged asset is not established: the CNB tiers use std::filesystem, not the platform loader.
